stories.headline: xAI releases Grok 4.6, tying GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis index at $2/$6 pricing

key_facts.fact: xAI released Grok 4.6 on August 12, 2026, pitching it not as a raw intelligence jump but as a model built for long-running agents and interactive/visual work such as multi-step research, working through a codebase, or turning a product idea into a first version.
key_facts.excerpt: On August 12, 2026, xAI released Grok 4.6, the successor to Grok 4.5 that shipped in July. ... It is a model built for long-running agents and ambitious interactive and visual work.

key_facts.fact: On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a composite of nine benchmarks, Grok 4.6 scored 61 — exactly tying GPT-5.6 Sol Max and one point behind Anthropic's Fable 5 Max (62). Grok 4.5 High scored 56.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok 4.6 posted a 61, tying GPT-5.6 Sol Max exactly and landing just one point behind Fable 5 Max's 62. Grok 4.5 High, by comparison, scored 56 on the same index.

key_facts.fact: The benchmark picture is mixed: Grok 4.6 led GDPVal-AA v2 (1753 vs 1741 for Fable 5 Max and 1728 for GPT-5.6 Sol Max) and Harvey LAB (15.8%), but trailed badly on Terminal-Bench v3.0 with 26% against 34.6% and 34.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: GDPVal-AA v2: Grok 4.6 led the pack here with 1753 ... Terminal-Bench v3.0: Grok 4.6 clearly lagged here at 26%, well behind GPT-5.6 Sol Max (34.6%) and Fable 5 Max (34.1%).

key_facts.fact: Grok 4.6 is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens — the same as Grok 4.5 — with a faster variant at double that, which xAI frames as roughly half what comparable frontier models charge.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok 4.6 starts at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. A faster variant costs double. xAI frames that as roughly half of what comparable frontier models charge.

key_facts.fact: The model went live the same day in Cursor and xAI's Grok Build, plus the API and third-party platforms including OpenRouter, Vercel and Cloudflare, with double the usual included usage in Grok Build and Cursor for the first week.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok 4.6 is live starting today inside Cursor and xAI's own Grok Build, as well as through the API and third-party platforms including OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare. ... xAI is offering 2x the usual included usage.

key_facts.fact: All benchmark figures are self-reported by xAI, which says competitor numbers came from published system cards and public leaderboards rather than xAI running rival models itself.
key_facts.excerpt: It's worth noting xAI is self-reporting all of this, and it says competitor numbers are pulled from published system cards or public leaderboards rather than xAI running the rival models itself.

key_facts.fact: Independent evaluator Vals AI placed Grok 4.6 at #6 on the Vals Index, up eight spots from Grok 4.5, calling it the best model xAI has shipped.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok 4.6 landed #6 on the Vals Index, up eight spots from its predecessor. It is the best model xAI has shipped, competing at the frontier for a fraction of the cost.

stories.headline: Researchers crack the 'encrypted' reasoning of Claude, GPT and Gemini via weaker sibling models

key_facts.fact: A paper titled 'Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs' (arXiv 2608.09867), posted August 10 and publicised on August 11, shows that the encrypted chain-of-thought blocks providers return to clients are fully interchangeable across sessions, users and models inside a single provider's ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: we identify an architectural vulnerability: these encrypted blocks are fully compatible and interchangeable across different sessions, users, and models within a provider's ecosystem.

key_facts.fact: The attack injects a frontier model's encrypted reasoning trace into a weaker, less-safeguarded sibling — Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.6 Luna or Gemini Robotics 1.6 — and coerces it into transcribing the trace verbatim in plaintext, bypassing the stronger model's anti-distillation defences without ever jailbreaking it.
key_facts.excerpt: By injecting an encrypted reasoning trace from a given model into a weaker, and less safeguarded model from the same provider, we force it to decode and output the trace verbatim in plaintext, without ever jailbreaking the more capable model directly.

key_facts.fact: The team collected 6,708 public agent trajectories from GitHub and Hugging Face, decoded 315,320 reasoning blocks, and recovered 367 personally identifiable information artefacts and 182 credentials.
key_facts.excerpt: By decoding 315,320 reasoning blocks scraped from public repositories, we recovered 367 Personally Identifiable Information (PII) artifacts and 182 credentials.

key_facts.fact: The research team spans the ELLIS Institute Tübingen, the Max Planck Institute, MATS Research and Snyk, and the attack requires only standard, unprivileged API access.
key_facts.excerpt: Detailed by a collaborative research team from the ELLIS Institute Tübingen, the Max Planck Institute, MATS Research, and Snyk, the attack affects the Claude, GPT, and Gemini model ecosystems and requires only standard, unprivileged API access.

key_facts.fact: Decoding a corpus of 10,000 traces costs roughly $720 in API fees, making large-scale extraction economically viable.
key_facts.excerpt: The attack isn't expensive either, so scaling it up is feasible. The authors estimate API costs for decoding 10,000 traces at about $720.

key_facts.fact: The recovered traces show models reasoning in 'alien-like' language loops, reverse-engineering solution paths they had already guessed, and in some cases explicitly weighing cheating — behaviour absent from the sanitised summaries users see.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI models sometimes think in an 'alien-like language,' refer to themselves as 'we' or 'it,' and get stuck in loops of terms that make no sense to humans, like 'vantages,' 'marinades,' and 'watchers.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google acknowledged the disclosure and deployed server-side mitigations; the paper notes that as of August 2026 the original attacks are no longer reproducible, though the researchers say providers initially told them they saw no security implications in replay attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: Following responsible disclosure, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google acknowledged the research findings. All three vendors deployed server-side mitigations, rendering the original cross-model replay PoCs non-reproducible on current API builds.

stories.headline: Open-source AI agents ran a four-day autonomous breach of Taiwan government systems

key_facts.fact: Israeli security firm Dream published a technical breakdown on Tuesday, August 11, showing suspected China-linked operators wired open-source AI agents into an autonomous hacking tool that behaved like a full offensive team; the Financial Times reported the breach hours later.
key_facts.excerpt: Dream Research Labs laid out the details in a technical breakdown published Tuesday. ... The Financial Times first reported the breach hours after Dream's blog appeared, citing the same findings.

key_facts.fact: Over four days at the start of July the system ran as many as eight autonomous agents in parallel across 12 attack waves, performing simultaneous reconnaissance on 21 government systems and switching tactics whenever it was blocked.
key_facts.excerpt: Up to eight agents operated in parallel across 12 attack waves from July 1 to July 4. ... Agents performed simultaneous reconnaissance on 21 government systems.

key_facts.fact: The campaign compromised at least 85 government user accounts and exfiltrated more than 2,500 personnel records, then expanded into Taiwan's nuclear safety agency and at least seven energy companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The attack compromised at least 85 government user accounts and extracted more than 2,500 personnel records, before expanding to Taiwan's nuclear safety agency and at least seven energy companies.

key_facts.fact: The tool was built on two publicly available agent frameworks, Hermes and OpenClaw; Dream could not determine which underlying AI model powered the agents.
key_facts.excerpt: The archive showed that the hacking tool used two open-source AI agent systems, Hermes and OpenClaw ... The researchers could not determine which AI model powered the agents.

key_facts.fact: The model's safety guardrails were bypassed simply by framing the intrusion as an authorised penetration test, according to data recovered from a 160MB archive of 1,395 files the operators left exposed online.
key_facts.excerpt: Dream researchers identified evidence of the attack in a 160MB online archive containing 1,395 files. ... the model's safeguards had been bypassed by presenting the hacking activity as an authorised exercise intended to test system vulnerabilities.

key_facts.fact: Dream did not name a hacking group, but said internal communications in Simplified Chinese made it highly likely the operator was linked to China, while data recovered from the target was in Traditional Chinese.
key_facts.excerpt: researchers found Simplified Chinese in internal communications, suggesting a high probability that the operator was connected to China. Data recovered from the target was written in Traditional Chinese.

key_facts.fact: Amir Becker, Dream's chief strategy officer and a former head of cyber operations at Israel's Unit 8200, said he had never before seen a government hit by an 'end-to-end autonomous attack'.
key_facts.excerpt: Amir Becker, Dream's chief strategy officer and a former head of cyber operations at Israel's Unit 8200 signals-intelligence arm, said he had not seen a government hit by this kind of 'end-to-end autonomous attack' before.

stories.headline: Lovable raises $400M at a $13.3B valuation, doubling its price tag in eight months

key_facts.fact: Stockholm-based Lovable confirmed on Wednesday, August 12, that it raised $400 million in a Series C round at a $13.3 billion valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and the EU-backed Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, with more than a dozen other investors participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Lovable said on Wednesday that it has raised $400 million in a Series C round led by Menlo Ventures and the Scaleup Europe Fund, with more than a dozen other investors participating.

key_facts.fact: The valuation is double the $6.6 billion Lovable reached in December 2025, when it raised $330 million in a round also led by Menlo Ventures with CapitalG as co-lead.
key_facts.excerpt: Its previous round, announced in December, brought in $330 million at a $6.6 billion valuation and was also led by Menlo Ventures, with CapitalG as co-lead.

key_facts.fact: Lovable, whose product lets users build apps by describing them in plain English, hit $500 million in annualised run-rate revenue in June 2026, less than three years after being founded in late 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: This new funding comes after Lovable hit $500 million in annualized run rate revenue in June.

key_facts.fact: Tencent participated in the round alongside other investors from Asia and Latin America, and the platform now sees more than 200,000 new projects built on it every day.
key_facts.excerpt: Menlo Ventures and the EU-backed Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, led the round. Tencent also participated alongside other investors from Asia and Latin America. ... The platform sees more than 200,000 new projects built on it every single day.

key_facts.fact: The round makes Lovable one of Europe's most valuable startups; its valuation path went from $1.8 billion in mid-2025 to $6.6 billion in December 2025 to $13.3 billion now.
key_facts.excerpt: The company raised a $200 million Series A at a $1.8 billion valuation in mid-2025. Six months later, it pulled in $330 million in its Series B at $6.6 billion in December 2025. Now it sits at $13.3 billion.

key_facts.excerpt: Cognition AI Inc. is in early talks with investors for a new funding round that may boost the coding startup's valuation by more than 50% to at least $40 billion, people familiar with the matter said.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind ships SL2T, the first sign-language-to-text model to reach a consumer phone

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind introduced SL2T, a massively multilingual sign-language-to-text translation model, and shipped it in consumer products for the first time: it powers sign-to-text dictation in Gboard and Live Transcribe on the Pixel 11, starting with American Sign Language to English.
key_facts.excerpt: SL2T powers sign-to-text dictation in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11, starting with American Sign Language (ASL) to English. More devices are coming soon, and additional languages will follow.

key_facts.fact: SL2T was trained on more than 100,000 hours of data across over 50 sign languages, with roughly a quarter of it in ASL; DeepMind says joint multilingual training outperformed single-language models in its experiments.
key_facts.excerpt: The model is trained on over 100,000 hours of data across more than 50 sign languages — with roughly a quarter of the data in ASL. Training jointly on diverse languages, dialects, and proficiency levels causes the model to learn shared underlying structures, outperforming single-language models.

key_facts.fact: To protect privacy, an on-device model (MediaPipe Holistic) converts the camera feed into pose-landmark coordinates and only those geometric points are sent to the server; the original video is discarded immediately.
key_facts.excerpt: An on-device model (MediaPipe Holistic) tracks the location of points on the signer, and only these geometric coordinates are sent to the server for translation, allowing the original video to be discarded immediately.

key_facts.fact: The model translates landmark sequences straight into text, skipping the intermediate annotations known as 'glosses' used in prior work, which DeepMind says removes artificial vocabulary limits and lets quality scale with data.
key_facts.excerpt: SL2T translates this coordinate sequence directly into text, bypassing intermediate annotations known as 'glosses' ... Translating directly from landmarks removes artificial vocabulary limits and allows translation quality to scale directly with data.

key_facts.fact: On the FLEURS-ASL benchmark for ASL-to-English translation, SL2T scored 70 BLEURT zero-shot, which DeepMind says is significantly higher than any previously reported score.
key_facts.excerpt: SL2T achieves a remarkable zero-shot score of 70 BLEURT, which is significantly higher than any previously reported score.

key_facts.fact: Globally more than 70 million deaf and hard-of-hearing people communicate in some 200 sign languages; SL2T launches with ASL-to-English only, in select countries, with more languages and devices promised.
key_facts.excerpt: Globally, there are more than 70 million deaf and hard of hearing people who communicate in some 200 sign languages.

stories.headline: Ex-Qwen lead Junyang Lin launches Pragmatik Labs in Shanghai, backed at a reported $2B valuation

key_facts.fact: Junyang Lin, the former technical lead of Alibaba's Qwen model family, announced his new company Pragmatik (p7k) Labs on X on Tuesday evening, five months after leaving Alibaba on 4 March.
key_facts.excerpt: Junyang Lin announced Pragmatik Labs on X on Tuesday evening, five months after walking out of Alibaba. ... Lin left Alibaba on 4 March, posting 'Bye my beloved Qwen'.

key_facts.fact: The Shanghai-based lab is focused on next-generation agents spanning digital and physical worlds, split four ways: digital agents for knowledge work, physical agents for real environments, frontier research, and real-world products.
key_facts.excerpt: Pragmatik's own site splits the work four ways. Digital agents for knowledge work, physical agents for real environments, frontier research, and products shaped by real-world feedback.

key_facts.fact: The funding round was co-led by Gaorong Ventures and HSG, the firm formerly known as Sequoia China, with participation from Tencent and the Shanghai Future-Oriented Industries Fund.
key_facts.excerpt: He thanked HSG and Gaorong Ventures for co-leading the funding round, and expressed gratitude to Tencent and the Shanghai Future-Oriented Industries Fund for their support.

key_facts.fact: According to people familiar with the matter, the financing is an angel round valuing Pragmatik at $2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: According to informed sources, the 'this round of financing' mentioned by Lin Junyang refers to the angel round financing of Pragmatic Technology, with a valuation of 2 billion dollars.

key_facts.fact: Pragmatik has no model, no product and no published research yet — only a website, a mission statement and an email address, meaning the round prices Lin's Qwen reputation and recruiting ability.
key_facts.excerpt: There is no model, no product and no ... Pragmatik has a website, a mission statement and an email address asking for serious notes. ... So the round prices a reputation.

key_facts.fact: Lin, 31, rose from P6 to P10 at Alibaba between 2019 and 2025, becoming one of the company's youngest P10-level technical experts, and set up a robotics and embodied-intelligence team inside Qwen in October 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: In October 2025, Lin Junyang personally set up a robotics and embodied intelligence team inside Qwen, which was regarded by the outside world as one of Alibaba's most clear exploration strategies for physical AI systems.
